Description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study on the Quranic verses regarding fasting in Sura 2, beginning with verses 183 to 187. He argues that fasting was originally decreed through Abraham and initially prohibited sexual intercourse for the entire month of Ramadan, a rule later relaxed in verse 187. He challenges the traditional belief that the Quran was revealed over 23 years, asserting instead that the entire text was placed into Muhammad's heart on the Night of Power, citing Suras 44, 53, and 97, while Gabriel merely supervised its gradual release. Dean Mahmoud and an unnamed man raise questions about how companions distinguished revelation from ordinary speech, prompting Khalifa to reject traditional accounts of Muhammad fainting or experiencing epileptic symptoms. He references the spelling of Becca with a "B" in Sura 3:96 as proof of divine preservation, arguing the mathematical structure would collapse with an "M." Khalifa also critiques Abul A'la Maududi's theory on the Quranic initials, noting they only appear in 29 chapters. Discussing the physical demands of fasting and the Fajr prayer, he explains that the Earth's tilted axis and shifting seasons are designed to test the believers' commitment. He compares the body to a wild horse that must be tamed by the soul, quoting the General Electric motto to emphasize spiritual progress. He concludes with an anecdote about a car accident in Tripoli, Libya, which disproved his own theory that God takes three to six months to answer prayers.
